documents.title: Optional Syllabus Statements for the Acceptable or Unacceptable Use of AI Tools in Your Course
documents.summary: A set of four optional sample syllabus statements from the Academic Senate, from broad permission to a full ban, that instructors adapt and fill in with a penalty. It also tells instructors to be specific about permitted activities and to think about penalties. It sets no campus-wide rule itself.
documents.stance_why: The document offers four template statements for instructors to adjust ('Please adjust the statement to reflect your parameters'), spanning 'You are welcome to use generative AI tools' to 'is not permitted in this class'. It sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates with the templates listed as tiers.

units.why: Unacceptable statement 2 bans AI only 'for the following activities', so the ban is activity-level and set by the instructor, P04.

units.why: The sample statements are offered for instructors to 'adjust ... to reflect your parameters and to fit your course', so the rule is set per course by the instructor; P04 fits better than P09 because the point is who decides, not that a statement is mandatory.

documents.title: Student Guidelines on Generative AI
documents.summary: A student-facing page explaining that instructors may allow broad, specific or no AI use, and that students must check the syllabus and ask before using AI. It requires citation of permitted use, warns of discipline for unauthorized use, and notes AI features in ordinary software count. It raises equity and sustainability concerns.
documents.stance_why: Coder A coded restrict, coder B delegates. Although instructors decide per course, the page's operative rule is 'DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor', so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted: restrict rather than delegates, since the student-facing default is no AI without permission. The page ends its guidance with "DO NOT use GenAI unless you have received an OK from your instructor", a default ban unless the instructor permits, which is restrict; it is not delegates because the document itself sets that default.
